contexts.context: The excerpt does not specifically identify or describe the Constellium patents WO2020095009A2 and EP3914748B1, nor does it provide their individual examples. It does, however, describe a related heat-resistant aluminum alloy powder intended for additive manufacturing. Its disclosed composition is nickel 2.5–5.5 wt%, manganese 1.0–3.5 wt%, iron 0.15–2.0 wt%, zirconium 0.2–1.0 wt%, and cerium 0.05–0.4 wt%. It also contains, in total, 0.05–1.5 wt% of at least one of copper, magnesium, and zinc, and 0.1–2.0 wt% of at least one of silicon and calcium; aluminum and unavoidable impurities form the balance. A preferred relationship is Ni > Mn + Fe. The material is designed for good printability, fluidity, and resistance to hot cracking, while targeting an ultimate tensile strength of at least 350 MPa at room temperature after printing. The alloy is intended to retain performance up to approximately 300–350°C and maintain strength after stress-relief annealing. Zirconium refines grains and forms thermally stable Al3Zr dispersoids, while iron forms Al9FeNi-type spherical particles and contributes to elevated-temperature strengthening without substantially reducing ductility.

contexts.question:
Survey the PATENT literature and COMMERCIAL products for aluminium alloys designed for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF / SLM) and related powder routes, so that we can choose starting compositions for an alloy discovery campaign and know what is already claimed. We want published compositions, not marketing.

For each entry give: assignee / vendor, product name if any, patent or application numbers (US, EP, WO, CN, JP, DE), priority year, the claimed composition RANGES and the worked EXAMPLE compositions (wt%), the cracking-control and strengthening mechanism claimed, recommended heat treatment, the properties reported in the patent or datasheet (yield, UTS, elongation, hardness, conductivity, test orientation), and whether the patent is granted, pending, expired or abandoned where known.

Cover at least:
1. Airbus / APWorks Scalmalloy (Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn), and the earlier Al-Mg-Sc family patents; lower-Sc or Sc-free variants claimed by others.
2. HRL Laboratories 7A77 and Zr / grain-refiner functionalized 7xxx, 6xxx, 2xxx powders.
3. Aeromet / Aluminium Materials Technologies A20X (A205; Al-Cu-Ag-Mg-Ti-B).
4. NanoAl / Unity Aluminum / Braidy Addalloy (Al-Mg-Zr and others) and Northwestern University Al-Zr-(Er, Sc, Yb, Si) patents.
5. Constellium Aheadd CP1 (Al-Fe-Zr) and HT1 (Al-Ni-Mn-Cu-Zr-Fe class), and the C-TEC patent families (Al-Zr, Al-Fe-Zr, Al-Ni-Zr, Al-Mn-Zr, Al-Cr-Zr).
6. Fehrmann AlMgty (Al-Mg-Si / high-Mg), Rheinfelden (Magsimal, Castasil, Castaduct for AM), AMAG, Hydro, Trimet.
7. Elementum 3D A1000-RAM, A2024-RAM2, A6061-RAM2, A7050-RAM2 (reactive additive manufacturing, in-situ ceramic inoculants).
8. Rusal / IL&M (RS-230, RS-300, RS-320, RS-333, RS-390, RS-553 and similar: Al-Si-Mg-Cu, Al-Mg-Sc, Al-Ni-Mn-Fe-Zr, Al-Cu-Ce), with compositions.
9. Monash University / Amaero high-strength Al-Mn-Sc ("HOT Al"), and Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr.

Instead, it presents clauses for a different high-temperature aluminum alloy based on an aluminum matrix containing over 80 molar% aluminum and L12 precipitates of Al3M, where M includes erbium and zirconium. Its stated broad composition ranges are up to 2 molar% nickel, 0.1–1.5 molar% zirconium, and 0.1–1 molar% erbium, with erbium no greater than zirconium. A more specific composition is also listed as 1.204–1.332 molar% nickel, 0.393–0.401 molar% for one rare-earth component, and 0.894–1.005 molar% for the other, although the labels for zirconium and erbium appear transposed in the excerpt. Optional additions include yttrium or ytterbium up to 0.1%, and additional L12-forming elements such as scandium, thulium, lutetium, uranium, and neptunium. The alloy is described as having nanoscale L12 phases, high-temperature hardness, and yield strength of at least 400 MPa. These data may be useful for comparison but do not establish the composition ranges or example compositions of the requested Al–Mn patent.

contexts.context: The excerpt concerns a different patent and alloy system from the Farkoosh US12104237B2 patent identified in the question. It describes an Al–Mn–Sc alloy intended for additive manufacturing and other rapid-solidification processes. Within this excerpt, manganese is described as usable from 2.01 wt% up to 15.0 wt%, with levels above 15 wt% potentially causing undesirable precipitate coarsening. The alloy also uses scandium and may include zirconium, relying on rapid solidification and subsequent precipitation of thermally stable nanoscale precipitates or dispersoids. The reported laser-remelted material reached 170–186 HV0.5 and retained high hardness after 168 hours at 300°C. Tensile testing produced a yield strength of 427 MPa in the as-fabricated condition and 577 MPa after heat treatment. However, the excerpt does not provide the composition ranges or example compositions of the specific Farkoosh ultra-strong Al–Mn alloy with L12 precipitates. It therefore supplies only potentially related background on Al–Mn-based additive-manufacturing alloys, not the requested patent’s actual formulation details.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes an Al–Mn–Si alloy family modified with one or more low concentrations of Sn, In, Sb, and/or Bi. The principal composition ranges are 0.3–0.7 at.% Mn and about 0.2–1.0 at.% Si, with the Sn/In/Sb/Bi addition preferably about 0.01–0.02 at.%. Iron may be present at impurity levels up to about 0.3 at.%. Optional alloying additions include Ga (up to 0.01 at.%), Cu (about 0.01–0.1 at.%), Ti (up to 0.01–0.11 at.%), V (up to 0.01–0.05 at.%), Cr (up to 0.01–0.10 at.%), Zr (about 0.01–0.1 at.%), and Zn (about 0.01–0.3 at.%). Examples include a Sn-modified alloy containing about 0.6 at.% Si, reported with approximately 650 MPa peak microhardness, and a Sn-modified alloy containing 0.09 at.% Zr and 0.3 at.% Si, reported with approximately 725 MPa microhardness. The excerpt also identifies uniformly distributed β-Al(Mn,Fe)Si precipitates and tin-rich nanoprecipitates, but it does not provide a complete nominal composition for each example or establish the claimed L12 phase/additive-manufacturing aspect.

contexts.question:
Survey the PATENT literature and COMMERCIAL products for aluminium alloys designed for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF / SLM) and related powder routes, so that we can choose starting compositions for an alloy discovery campaign and know what is already claimed. We want published compositions, not marketing.

For each entry give: assignee / vendor, product name if any, patent or application numbers (US, EP, WO, CN, JP, DE), priority year, the claimed composition RANGES and the worked EXAMPLE compositions (wt%), the cracking-control and strengthening mechanism claimed, recommended heat treatment, the properties reported in the patent or datasheet (yield, UTS, elongation, hardness, conductivity, test orientation), and whether the patent is granted, pending, expired or abandoned where known.

Cover at least:
1. Airbus / APWorks Scalmalloy (Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn), and the earlier Al-Mg-Sc family patents; lower-Sc or Sc-free variants claimed by others.
2. HRL Laboratories 7A77 and Zr / grain-refiner functionalized 7xxx, 6xxx, 2xxx powders.
3. Aeromet / Aluminium Materials Technologies A20X (A205; Al-Cu-Ag-Mg-Ti-B).
4. NanoAl / Unity Aluminum / Braidy Addalloy (Al-Mg-Zr and others) and Northwestern University Al-Zr-(Er, Sc, Yb, Si) patents.
5. Constellium Aheadd CP1 (Al-Fe-Zr) and HT1 (Al-Ni-Mn-Cu-Zr-Fe class), and the C-TEC patent families (Al-Zr, Al-Fe-Zr, Al-Ni-Zr, Al-Mn-Zr, Al-Cr-Zr).
6. Fehrmann AlMgty (Al-Mg-Si / high-Mg), Rheinfelden (Magsimal, Castasil, Castaduct for AM), AMAG, Hydro, Trimet.
7. Elementum 3D A1000-RAM, A2024-RAM2, A6061-RAM2, A7050-RAM2 (reactive additive manufacturing, in-situ ceramic inoculants).
8. Rusal / IL&M (RS-230, RS-300, RS-320, RS-333, RS-390, RS-553 and similar: Al-Si-Mg-Cu, Al-Mg-Sc, Al-Ni-Mn-Fe-Zr, Al-Cu-Ce), with compositions.
9. Monash University / Amaero high-strength Al-Mn-Sc ("HOT Al"), and Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr.
10. Chalmers / Hoganas Al-Mn-Cr-Zr; Hoganas forAM Al grades; Kymera / ECKA / AP&C / Equispheres / Valimet / Carpenter / Sandvik / Toyal / Eckart (e.g. Eckart TiB2- or Zr-modified, Toyal Hyper-Al) aluminium AM powders with published chemistries.
11. Oak Ridge / Eck Industries / Ames Al-Ce alloys (Al-Ce-Mg, Al-Ce-Ni-Mn, Al-Cu-Mn-Zr / ACMZ, DuAlumin-3D), Lawrence Livermore Al-Ce.
12. Alcoa / Arconic / Howmet AM aluminium (Al-Fe-V-Si, Al-Ni, Al-Mn, "A1000" class), QuesTek Al for AM (Sc-free, high-temperature), Citrine / HRL / NASA collaborations, NASA 7xxx / GRCop is out of scope.
13. Japanese and Korean filings: Toyo Aluminium, Daido, Kobe Steel, UACJ, Nippon Light Metal, Sumitomo, Hitachi Metals, Toyota (Al-Fe, Al-Fe-Mn, Al-Fe-Cu, Al-Ni-Co, Al-Mn-Cr, Al-Si-Mg-Mn high-Mg).
14. Chinese filings and products: CRRC / Central South University Al-Mg-Sc-Zr, Al-Mg-Er-Zr (Beijing University of Technology Er-microalloying patents), Al-Mn-Mg-Er-Zr, TiB2/AlSi10Mg (Shanghai Jiao Tong), Al-Zn-Mg-Sc-Zr, Sc-free high-strength Al for AM.
15. EOS (Al2139 AM, Al5X1, AlF357), SLM Solutions / Nikon SLM, 3D Systems (A6061-RAM2 licence), Colibrium / GE Additive, Mercury Marine (Mercalloy A362 for AM), Gränges (Dispal-type Al-Si-Fe-Ni), PEAK Werkstoff / Erbslöh (Dispal S220/S250 Al-Si), Kaiser, Novelis, Uniformity Labs.
16. Any patents specifically on aluminium powders made by ULTRASONIC atomization or small-batch atomization for alloy development.

Then answer:
A. Which claimed composition windows overlap a search space of Al >= 85 wt% with a few additions from Mn, Cr, Zr, Mg, Si, Cu, Ti, Fe, Ni, Ce, Sc, Li, Er, Zn, Sn? Where is there apparent white space (combinations nobody has claimed or published), especially Sc-free and with little or no Zr?
B. Which commercial Sc-free alloys have the highest reported yield strength at >= 8 % elongation, and what do their datasheets give for as-built versus heat-treated?
C. Which patent example compositions would make good seed experiments for us, given feedstock on hand (Al, Si, Mg, Mn, Cr, Zn, Sn, Ti, small Sc and Er; Fe, Cu and Ni easy to buy; Zr uncertain)?
D. Anything in these patents about atomization practice (melt temperature, superheat for Zr/Ti/Cr/Mn-bearing melts, crucible materials, Mg loss) or about build-plate preheat that we should copy.

Give patent numbers and URLs or DOIs for every claim. Say clearly when a composition comes from a datasheet, a patent example, a patent claim range, or a journal paper by the same group.

For each entry give: assignee / vendor, product name if any, patent or application numbers (US, EP, WO, CN, JP, DE), priority year, the claimed composition RANGES and the worked EXAMPLE compositions (wt%), the cracking-control and strengthening mechanism claimed, recommended heat treatment, the properties reported in the patent or datasheet (yield, UTS, elongation, hardness, conductivity, test orientation), and whether the patent is granted, pending, expired or abandoned where known.

Cover at least:
1. Airbus / APWorks Scalmalloy (Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn), and the earlier Al-Mg-Sc family patents; lower-Sc or Sc-free variants claimed by others.
2. HRL Laboratories 7A77 and Zr / grain-refiner functionalized 7xxx, 6xxx, 2xxx powders.
3. Aeromet / Aluminium Materials Technologies A20X (A205; Al-Cu-Ag-Mg-Ti-B).
4. NanoAl / Unity Aluminum / Braidy Addalloy (Al-Mg-Zr and others) and Northwestern University Al-Zr-(Er, Sc, Yb, Si) patents.
5. Constellium Aheadd CP1 (Al-Fe-Zr) and HT1 (Al-Ni-Mn-Cu-Zr-Fe class), and the C-TEC patent families (Al-Zr, Al-Fe-Zr, Al-Ni-Zr, Al-Mn-Zr, Al-Cr-Zr).
6. Fehrmann AlMgty (Al-Mg-Si / high-Mg), Rheinfelden (Magsimal, Castasil, Castaduct for AM), AMAG, Hydro, Trimet.
7. Elementum 3D A1000-RAM, A2024-RAM2, A6061-RAM2, A7050-RAM2 (reactive additive manufacturing, in-situ ceramic inoculants).
8. Rusal / IL&M (RS-230, RS-300, RS-320, RS-333, RS-390, RS-553 and similar: Al-Si-Mg-Cu, Al-Mg-Sc, Al-Ni-Mn-Fe-Zr, Al-Cu-Ce), with compositions.
9. Monash University / Amaero high-strength Al-Mn-Sc ("HOT Al"), and Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr.
10. Chalmers / Hoganas Al-Mn-Cr-Zr; Hoganas forAM Al grades; Kymera / ECKA / AP&C / Equispheres / Valimet / Carpenter / Sandvik / Toyal / Eckart (e.g. Eckart TiB2- or Zr-modified, Toyal Hyper-Al) aluminium AM powders with published chemistries.
11. Oak Ridge / Eck Industries / Ames Al-Ce alloys (Al-Ce-Mg, Al-Ce-Ni-Mn, Al-Cu-Mn-Zr / ACMZ, DuAlumin-3D), Lawrence Livermore Al-Ce.
12. Alcoa / Arconic / Howmet AM aluminium (Al-Fe-V-Si, Al-Ni, Al-Mn, "A1000" class), QuesTek Al for AM (Sc-free, high-temperature), Citrine / HRL / NASA collaborations, NASA 7xxx / GRCop is out of scope.
13. Japanese and Korean filings: Toyo Aluminium, Daido, Kobe Steel, UACJ, Nippon Light Metal, Sumitomo, Hitachi Metals, Toyota (Al-Fe, Al-Fe-Mn, Al-Fe-Cu, Al-Ni-Co, Al-Mn-Cr, Al-Si-Mg-Mn high-Mg).
14. Chinese filings and products: CRRC / Central South University Al-Mg-Sc-Zr, Al-Mg-Er-Zr (Beijing University of Technology Er-microalloying patents), Al-Mn-Mg-Er-Zr, TiB2/AlSi10Mg (Shanghai Jiao Tong), Al-Zn-Mg-Sc-Zr, Sc-free high-strength Al for AM.
15. EOS (Al2139 AM, Al5X1, AlF357), SLM Solutions / Nikon SLM, 3D Systems (A6061-RAM2 licence), Colibrium / GE Additive, Mercury Marine (Mercalloy A362 for AM), Gränges (Dispal-type Al-Si-Fe-Ni), PEAK Werkstoff / Erbslöh (Dispal S220/S250 Al-Si), Kaiser, Novelis, Uniformity Labs.
16. Any patents specifically on aluminium powders made by ULTRASONIC atomization or small-batch atomization for alloy development.

Then answer:
A. Which claimed composition windows overlap a search space of Al >= 85 wt% with a few additions from Mn, Cr, Zr, Mg, Si, Cu, Ti, Fe, Ni, Ce, Sc, Li, Er, Zn, Sn? Where is there apparent white space (combinations nobody has claimed or published), especially Sc-free and with little or no Zr?
B. Which commercial Sc-free alloys have the highest reported yield strength at >= 8 % elongation, and what do their datasheets give for as-built versus heat-treated?
C. Which patent example compositions would make good seed experiments for us, given feedstock on hand (Al, Si, Mg, Mn, Cr, Zn, Sn, Ti, small Sc and Er; Fe, Cu and Ni easy to buy; Zr uncertain)?
D. Anything in these patents about atomization practice (melt temperature, superheat for Zr/Ti/Cr/Mn-bearing melts, crucible materials, Mg loss) or about build-plate preheat that we should copy.

Give patent numbers and URLs or DOIs for every claim. Say clearly when a composition comes from a datasheet, a patent example, a patent claim range, or a journal paper by the same group.

contexts.context: The excerpt discusses Scalmalloy® as an LPBF aluminium alloy whose strength derives from grain-boundary strengthening, Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitation hardening, solid-solution strengthening, and dislocation density. It describes a bimodal fine-grained/coarse-grained microstructure: fine-grained regions provide greater Hall–Petch strengthening, while coarse-grained regions can accommodate more dislocations and therefore improve ductility. Reported Hall–Petch contributions are 139–166 MPa for fine-grained zones and 78–96 MPa for coarse-grained zones, with another study reporting 195–215 MPa. Direct-aged material retains high yield strength and ultimate tensile strength because of the bimodal microstructure and precipitates. Exposure near 500 °C coarsens or recrystallizes the microstructure and substantially reduces strength, while ductility is influenced by grain-zone morphology, precipitates, and grain-boundary intermetallic phases. The excerpt also states that 300–325 °C treatments relax residual stresses and promote Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitation. It does not provide the nominal Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn composition or the numerical yield-strength, UTS, and elongation values for as-built and heat-treated conditions; those values would need to be obtained from Table 3, Figure 17, or another section of the review.

contexts.context: The review identifies Scalmalloy® as a hypereutectic aluminum alloy with the nominal alloying system Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn. Its principal strengthening elements are Sc and Zr: fine Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates form during direct aging, while Al3Sc seed crystals promote grain refinement. Zr also helps resist precipitate coarsening and recrystallization at temperatures below 500 °C. In the as-built LPBF condition, the alloy has a bimodal fine/coarse-grain microstructure and generally isotropic mechanical behavior. Reported as-built properties are yield strength (YS) of 256–278 MPa, ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 349–350 MPa, and elongation of 19.0–20.0%; another cited measurement gives YS 268 ± 7 MPa, UTS 353 ± 4 MPa, and elongation 21 ± 1%. Direct aging at 325 °C for 4 h increases YS to 456–469 MPa and UTS to 512–521 MPa, while reducing elongation to 12.0–13.0%, largely preserving the bimodal microstructure. HIP at 325 °C for 4 h and 1000 bar reduces porosity to approximately 0.18% and further raises YS to 482–493 MPa and UTS to 523–547 MPa. The excerpt does not provide numerical nominal weight percentages for Al, Mg, Sc, Zr, and Mn.

snippets: Scalmalloy® is an Al-Mg-Sc-Zr alloy designed for the additive manufacturing of components used in various industrial applications.
The as-built alloy shows yield strength values of 256–278 MPa, ultimate tensile strength of 349–350 MPa, and elongation of 19.0–20.0%
After direct aging heat treatment (325 ◦C × 4 h), the yield and ultimate tensile strength values increase up to 456–469 MPa and 512–521 MPa, respectively, while the strain decreases to 12.0–13.0%
The HIP treatment, carried out at 325 ◦C × 4 h with a pressure of 1000 bar, reduced the porosity (approximatively 0.18%)
The yield strength and the ultimate tensile strength rose to 482–493 MPa and 523–547 MPa, respectively.
Scalmalloy® is a hypereutectic Al-Mg-Sc alloy based on an Al-Sc system containing other alloying elements such as Zr, Mg, and Mn

contexts.context: The excerpt provides only a limited comparison with Scalmalloy. contexts.context: The excerpt identifies the principal alloy composition as Al-6Mg-0.7Mn-0.4Er-1.2Zr (wt.%), a Sc-free, Er-containing alloy processed by LPBF at Beijing University of Technology. It states that increasing Er reduces crack density, while primary L12-Al3Zr promotes heterogeneous nucleation, equiaxed grain formation, and grain refinement, thereby suppressing solidification cracking. During aging, early Al3Er precipitation promotes Zr precipitation and produces an Al3(Er,Zr) core-shell structure, increasing precipitation strengthening. For the highlighted composition, the reported heat-treated/aged properties were a yield strength of 440 ± 3 MPa, tensile strength of 520 ± 2 MPa, and elongation of 15.5 ± 1.0%; the abstract also describes the strength as exceeding 500 MPa after heat treatment. contexts.context: The excerpt provides composition and property information for Farkoosh US12104237B2, but it does not provide the QuesTek patent or US20260002237A1 (Mousavi), nor does it explicitly identify L12 precipitates. Farkoosh’s alloys are aluminum–manganese–silicon alloys modified with Sn, In, Sb, and/or Bi. The disclosed ranges are approximately 0.3–0.7 at.% Mn, 0.2–1.0 at.% Si, and preferably 0.01–0.02 at.% of the Sn/In/Sb/Bi additions. Optional additions include Zr at about 0.01–0.1 at.% and Fe up to about 0.3 at.%, with other possible alloying elements including Cu, Ti, V, Cr, and Zn. The alloys are described as castable, weldable, brazeable, and heat-treatable, with thermal stability and resistance to creep, coarsening, and recrystallization. Reported peak microhardness values include about 525 MPa, about 650 MPa for a Sn-modified alloy containing approximately 0.6 at.% Si, and about 725 MPa for a Sn-modified alloy containing 0.09 at.% Zr and 0.3 Si. Peak-aged β-Al(Mn,Fe)Si precipitates reportedly have number densities above 10^22 m−3 and mean radii below 25 nm; tin-rich nanoprecipitates have a mean radius of about 1.5 nm. The excerpt therefore supports Farkoosh data only and is insufficient for a three-patent comparison or confirmation of L12 chemistry.

It concerns a different patent, US11603583B2, assigned to NanoAL LLC, but it does describe a potentially relevant high-temperature aluminum-alloy approach involving L1₂ precipitates. The disclosed alloys use aluminum as the balance, 1–10 wt.% magnesium, 0.3–3 wt.% zirconium (preferably 0.45–3 wt.%), and optionally 0.3–1.5 wt.% vanadium. They contain both micron-scale primary Al₃Zr precipitates formed during rapid solidification and 3–50 nm Al₃Zr nanoprecipitates with an L1₂ crystal structure formed during aging. The patent attributes high room- and elevated-temperature strength, creep resistance, corrosion resistance, ductility, weldability, and heat resistance up to approximately 400°C to this microstructure. It further states that the Al₃Zr precipitates remain stable and resistant to coarsening up to 425°C. The alloys are described as scandium-free or containing no more than 0.05 wt.% incidental scandium, and as having a thermal extrusion window up to 450°C. These details may serve as background for comparison, but the excerpt contains no specific information about the three patents named in the question.

contexts.context: The excerpt provides detailed information for the Mousavi patent (US20260002237A1), but it does not contain composition or property information for the QuesTek or Farkoosh US12104237B2 patents. Mousavi describes an aluminum alloy containing an aluminum matrix with more than 80 molar% aluminum and L12 Al3M precipitates, where M includes erbium and zirconium; the precipitates are no larger than 20 nm. A broader composition includes up to 2 molar% nickel, 0.1–1.5 molar% zirconium, and 0.1–1 molar% erbium, with erbium not exceeding zirconium. Nickel may occur as Al3Ni precipitate. The alloy may additionally contain yttrium or ytterbium up to 0.1%, and can include other L12-forming elements. Stated properties include freedom from hot cracking, surface hardness above 150 HV (or above 175 HV), retention of hardness above 150 HV after at least 8 hours at 400°C, and yield strength of at least 400 MPa. L12 precipitates in the 16–20 nm range are associated with low-creep performance. Fabrication uses rapid solidification at at least 100 K/s followed by aging below the solvus temperature.

Question: Survey the PATENT literature and COMMERCIAL products for aluminium alloys designed for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF / SLM) and related powder routes, so that we can choose starting compositions for an alloy discovery campaign and know what is already claimed. We want published compositions, not marketing.

For each entry give: assignee / vendor, product name if any, patent or application numbers (US, EP, WO, CN, JP, DE), priority year, the claimed composition RANGES and the worked EXAMPLE compositions (wt%), the cracking-control and strengthening mechanism claimed, recommended heat treatment, the properties reported in the patent or datasheet (yield, UTS, elongation, hardness, conductivity, test orientation), and whether the patent is granted, pending, expired or abandoned where known.

Cover at least:
1. Airbus / APWorks Scalmalloy (Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn), and the earlier Al-Mg-Sc family patents; lower-Sc or Sc-free variants claimed by others.
2. HRL Laboratories 7A77 and Zr / grain-refiner functionalized 7xxx, 6xxx, 2xxx powders.
3. Aeromet / Aluminium Materials Technologies A20X (A205; Al-Cu-Ag-Mg-Ti-B).
4. NanoAl / Unity Aluminum / Braidy Addalloy (Al-Mg-Zr and others) and Northwestern University Al-Zr-(Er, Sc, Yb, Si) patents.
5. Constellium Aheadd CP1 (Al-Fe-Zr) and HT1 (Al-Ni-Mn-Cu-Zr-Fe class), and the C-TEC patent families (Al-Zr, Al-Fe-Zr, Al-Ni-Zr, Al-Mn-Zr, Al-Cr-Zr).
6. Fehrmann AlMgty (Al-Mg-Si / high-Mg), Rheinfelden (Magsimal, Castasil, Castaduct for AM), AMAG, Hydro, Trimet.
7. Elementum 3D A1000-RAM, A2024-RAM2, A6061-RAM2, A7050-RAM2 (reactive additive manufacturing, in-situ ceramic inoculants).
8. Rusal / IL&M (RS-230, RS-300, RS-320, RS-333, RS-390, RS-553 and similar: Al-Si-Mg-Cu, Al-Mg-Sc, Al-Ni-Mn-Fe-Zr, Al-Cu-Ce), with compositions.
9. Monash University / Amaero high-strength Al-Mn-Sc ("HOT Al"), and Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr.
10. Chalmers / Hoganas Al-Mn-Cr-Zr; Hoganas forAM Al grades; Kymera / ECKA / AP&C / Equispheres / Valimet / Carpenter / Sandvik / Toyal / Eckart (e.g. Eckart TiB2- or Zr-modified, Toyal Hyper-Al) aluminium AM powders with published chemistries.
11. Oak Ridge / Eck Industries / Ames Al-Ce alloys (Al-Ce-Mg, Al-Ce-Ni-Mn, Al-Cu-Mn-Zr / ACMZ, DuAlumin-3D), Lawrence Livermore Al-Ce.
12. Alcoa / Arconic / Howmet AM aluminium (Al-Fe-V-Si, Al-Ni, Al-Mn, "A1000" class), QuesTek Al for AM (Sc-free, high-temperature), Citrine / HRL / NASA collaborations, NASA 7xxx / GRCop is out of scope.
13. Japanese and Korean filings: Toyo Aluminium, Daido, Kobe Steel, UACJ, Nippon Light Metal, Sumitomo, Hitachi Metals, Toyota (Al-Fe, Al-Fe-Mn, Al-Fe-Cu, Al-Ni-Co, Al-Mn-Cr, Al-Si-Mg-Mn high-Mg).
14. Chinese filings and products: CRRC / Central South University Al-Mg-Sc-Zr, Al-Mg-Er-Zr (Beijing University of Technology Er-microalloying patents), Al-Mn-Mg-Er-Zr, TiB2/AlSi10Mg (Shanghai Jiao Tong), Al-Zn-Mg-Sc-Zr, Sc-free high-strength Al for AM.
15. EOS (Al2139 AM, Al5X1, AlF357), SLM Solutions / Nikon SLM, 3D Systems (A6061-RAM2 licence), Colibrium / GE Additive, Mercury Marine (Mercalloy A362 for AM), Gränges (Dispal-type Al-Si-Fe-Ni), PEAK Werkstoff / Erbslöh (Dispal S220/S250 Al-Si), Kaiser, Novelis, Uniformity Labs.
16. Any patents specifically on aluminium powders made by ULTRASONIC atomization or small-batch atomization for alloy development.

Then answer:
A. Which claimed composition windows overlap a search space of Al >= 85 wt% with a few additions from Mn, Cr, Zr, Mg, Si, Cu, Ti, Fe, Ni, Ce, Sc, Li, Er, Zn, Sn? Where is there apparent white space (combinations nobody has claimed or published), especially Sc-free and with little or no Zr?
B. Which commercial Sc-free alloys have the highest reported yield strength at >= 8 % elongation, and what do their datasheets give for as-built versus heat-treated?
C. Which patent example compositions would make good seed experiments for us, given feedstock on hand (Al, Si, Mg, Mn, Cr, Zn, Sn, Ti, small Sc and Er; Fe, Cu and Ni easy to buy; Zr uncertain)?
D. Anything in these patents about atomization practice (melt temperature, superheat for Zr/Ti/Cr/Mn-bearing melts, crucible materials, Mg loss) or about build-plate preheat that we should copy.

Give patent numbers and URLs or DOIs for every claim. Say clearly when a composition comes from a datasheet, a patent example, a patent claim range, or a journal paper by the same group.

# Survey of Aluminium Alloys Designed for Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF/SLM): Patent and Commercial Landscape

## 1. Introduction

This survey covers the patent and published-composition landscape for aluminium alloys specifically designed or adapted for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF / SLM) and related rapid-solidification powder routes. The objective is to identify claimed composition windows, worked example compositions, strengthening mechanisms, recommended heat treatments, and reported mechanical properties, so that starting compositions for a new alloy discovery campaign can be selected with knowledge of what is already claimed. The following sections are organized by alloy family, followed by an integrated analysis addressing white space, best Sc-free performers, recommended seed experiments, and atomization/processing guidance.

---

### 2.1 Airbus / APWorks — Scalmalloy® (Al–Mg–Sc–Zr–Mn)

The foundational Scalmalloy® patent family originates from Palm / EADS Deutschland GmbH, with the earliest priority around 2007 (WO2008/125092, DE102007018123). The atomization-related patent EP2766136B1 (priority 2011) claims nitrogen-rich atomization (50–100 vol% N₂) of Al–Sc alloys with the composition Mg 0.5–10, Sc 0.2–2.0, Zr 0.2–2.0 wt%, optionally with Mn 0.1–1.0, and a preferred sub-range of Mg 2.5–5.0, Sc 0.3–1.0, Zr 0.2–0.5, Mn 0.1–0.8 wt% (EP2766136B1 pages 3-5). The published Scalmalloy® composition used in research is Al–4.4Mg–0.8Sc–0.3Zr–0.5Mn wt% (schimback2022alloydesignstrategy pages 1-2). The composition range reported across studies is Mg 3.02–4.77, Sc 0.20–0.71, Mn 0.20–0.53, Zr 0.08–0.42 wt% (cerri2024mainheattreatments pages 2-5).

**Mechanism:** Primary Al₃(Sc,Zr) particles nucleate fine equiaxed grains at melt-pool boundaries, creating a bimodal microstructure that suppresses hot cracking. Direct aging precipitates coherent L1₂ Al₃(Sc,Zr) nanoprecipitates for strengthening (cerri2024mainheattreatments pages 1-2, cerri2024mainheattreatments pages 16-18).

**Properties (journal/review data):** As-built YS 256–278 MPa, UTS 349–350 MPa, El 19–20%; after direct aging at 325°C × 4 h: YS 456–469 MPa, UTS 512–521 MPa, El 12–13%; after HIP at 325°C/1000 bar: YS 482–493 MPa, UTS 523–547 MPa (cerri2024mainheattreatments pages 1-2, mehta2021laserpowderbed pages 7-10).

Airbus also developed **Scancromal®** (Al–2.6Cr–0.7Sc–0.3Zr, US20220186346A1) and **Scantital®** (Al–1.0Ti–1.0Sc–0.4Zr, US20220168811A1 with Ti 0.1–15, Sc 0.1–3.0, Zr 0.1–3.0 wt%) (schimback2022alloydesignstrategy pages 1-2, US20220168811A1 pages 4-5).

### 2.2 HRL Laboratories — Functionalized 7xxx/6xxx and 7A77-Type

HRL's core innovation is surface functionalization of conventional alloy powders with grain-refining nanoparticles. Key granted patents include US11053571B2, US11286543B2, and US11919085B2 (priority 2015–2017 family). The worked example uses Al 7075 powder (Al bal.–5.40Zn–2.25Mg–1.54Cu–0.19Cr–0.17Fe–0.13Si wt%) with ~1 vol% ZrH₂ nanoparticles (500–1500 nm), producing crack-free equiaxed microstructures via Al₃Zr heterogeneous nucleation (US11919085B2 pages 31-34, US20240082913A1 pages 64-66, US11053571B2 pages 32-33). T6 heat treatment: 480°C/2h, water quench, 120°C/18h (US11286543B2 pages 32-33).

The **7A77-type enriched feedstock** patent US11578389B2 (priority 2017, granted) claims a feedstock with Al 79.8–88.3, Cu 1.1–2.1, Mg 3.0–4.6, Zn 7.1–9.0, Zr 0.5–2.8 wt%, designed so that after ~25% Zn and ~30% Mg vaporization loss during LPBF, the printed part reaches Al 84.5–92.1, Cu 1.1–2.1, Mg 1.8–2.9, Zn 4.5–6.1, Zr 0.5–2.8 wt% (US11578389B2 pages 7-10, US11578389B2 pages 30-33).

### A. Composition Overlap and White Space

**Well-claimed regions (avoid as primary novelty):**
- Al–Mg–Sc–Zr(–Mn): Airbus Scalmalloy family (EP2766136B1 pages 3-5)
- Al–Zn–Mg–Cu–Zr: HRL (US11578389B2 pages 30-33), Snyder (US10941473B2 pages 21-22), Croteau (US20210254196A1 pages 11-12)
- Al–Fe–Zr: Constellium (WO2020095009A2 pages 1-4)
- Al–Ni–Mn–Fe–Zr–Ce: Rusal (CA3162961C pages 1-3)
- Al–Mn–Sc: Monash/Amaero (US11976343B2 pages 7-9)
- Al–Mg–Zr (Sc-free): NanoAl (US11603583B2 pages 18-20)

**Apparent white space for Sc-free, little/no Zr compositions with Al ≥ 85 wt%:**
- **Al–Mn–Mg–Cr** (no Sc, no Zr): No retrieved LPBF-specific patent claims this four-element core. Approximately Mn 1.5–4, Mg 1–4, Cr 0.3–1 wt% appears open.
- **Al–Mn–Cr–Si** (no Sc, no Zr): Relatively open except for Farkoosh's nearby Al–Mn–Si–Sn claims at low atomic %.
- **Al–Cu–Mn–Cr–Mg** (no Sc, no Zr): Not covered by retrieved AM claims.
- **Al–Mg–Si–Cr–Ti** (no Sc, no Zr): Open, though Ti grain refinement effectiveness needs validation.
- **Al–Mn–Cr–Fe–Si** (no Sc, no Zr, no RE): Open for a low-cost thermally stable family.

### B. Highest Sc-Free Yield Strength at ≥8% Elongation

The best verified Sc-free result is **Al–6Mg–0.7Mn–0.4Er–1.2Zr** from Beijing University of Technology (journal data): aged YS 440±3 MPa, UTS 520±2 MPa, El 15.5% (guo2022microstructureandmechanical pages 10-11, guo2022microstructureandmechanical pages 1-2). However, this alloy contains 1.2 wt% Zr and 0.4 wt% Er. Among alloys with no Sc and no/low Zr, no commercial datasheet with verified tensile data meeting the ≥8% elongation criterion was recovered. The Rusal RS-553-type achieves only 5.3% elongation at room temperature (CA3162961C pages 8-9).

### C. Recommended Seed Experiments

Given feedstock on hand (Al, Si, Mg, Mn, Cr, Zn, Sn, Ti, small Sc and Er; Fe, Cu, Ni easy; Zr uncertain):

1. **Al–6Mg–0.7Mn–0.4Er–1.2Zr** — Benchmark Sc-free recipe (requires Zr); age 375°C/10h (guo2022microstructureandmechanical pages 10-11).
2. **Al–4Mg–0.5Mn–0.3Sc–0.2Zr** — Low-Sc Scalmalloy control; age 300–325°C/4h (EP2766136B1 pages 3-5, cerri2024mainheattreatments pages 1-2).
3. **Al–3Mn–1.5Mg–0.5Cr–0.1Ti** — **High-priority white-space seed**, Sc/Zr-free; Mn/Cr solid-solution + dispersoid strengthening with Ti grain control.
4. **Al–5Mg–0.8Mn–0.5Si–0.3Cr–0.05Sn** — Farkoosh-inspired Sc/Zr-free precipitation concept; run Sn-free and 0.02/0.05 Sn variants (US12104237B2 pages 1-4).
5. **Al–3Mn–1.5Mg–0.6Cr–0.4Si–0.05Sn** — Lead Zr-free candidate combining white-space motifs; factorially vary Cr 0.3/0.6, Si 0.2/0.4, Sn 0/0.05.
6. **Al–7Zn–3Mg–1Cu–0.1Ti** — High-risk 7xxx control without Zr; consider TiB₂ inoculation.

### D. Atomization and Processing Guidance from Patents

- **Nitrogen atomization:** Airbus EP2766136B1 claims 50–100 vol% N₂ in atomizing gas for Al–Mg–Sc–Zr powders, producing an AlN-rich surface passivation layer that dramatically reduces moisture uptake versus conventional Al₂O₃. Conventional gas must be ≥99.99% purity with H₂O ≤25 ppm (EP2766136B1 pages 2-3, EP2766136B1 pages 3-5).
- **Mg/Zn vaporization loss:** HRL experimentally measured ~25% Zn and ~30% Mg loss during LPBF of 7075; enriched feedstock composition is claimed to compensate (US11578389B2 pages 7-10, US11578389B2 pages 30-33). These losses are machine- and parameter-specific.
- **Melt temperatures:** Croteau discloses melting at ~700–1000°C for Al–Zn–Mg–Zr alloys (US20210254196A1 pages 1-10). For Zr/Cr/Mn-bearing melts, use master alloys and verify dissolution; superheat should be established from the specific alloy liquidus.
- **LPBF parameter windows:** Rusal used EOS M290 at 280–320W, 400–1200 mm/s, ≤45 µm layers (CA3162961C pages 8-9). Monash used 370W, 1000 mm/s, 0.1 mm hatch, 30 µm layers (US11976343B2 pages 14-16).
- **Build-plate preheat:** No specific build-plate preheat temperature was recovered from the aluminium AM patents surveyed, though the Monash patent notes that direct aging can be performed before or after removal from the build platform (US11976343B2 pages 1-4).
- **Crucible materials and ultrasonic atomization:** No aluminium-specific crucible recommendation or directly applicable ultrasonic atomization protocol was recovered from the patent literature surveyed.

---

## 4. Limitations and Recommended Follow-Up

This survey covers the major patent families identified through systematic searching but has the following limitations:

1. **Incomplete extraction** of some patent families (Constellium EP4149702A2 HT1 compositions, Elementum 3D RAM, Fehrmann AlMgty, Japanese and Chinese filings) due to retrieval and time constraints.
2. **White space assessment is provisional** — a formal freedom-to-operate search with claim charting is required before filing or committing to a composition.
3. **Commercial datasheets** (EOS, SLM Solutions, Uniformity Labs, Höganäs forAM, Equispheres) were not retrieved as full documents; published compositions from these sources should be obtained directly from vendors.
4. The A20X (Al–Cu–Ag–Mg–Ti–B) patent family was not retrieved; the known composition (~Al–4.5Cu–0.3Ag–0.3Mg–0.2Ti–0.02B) should be confirmed against the original Aeromet/AMT filings.

The core finding is that Sc-free, Zr-free or low-Zr aluminium alloys based on **Al–Mn–Mg–Cr(–Si)** combinations represent the most promising apparent white space for a discovery campaign using the available feedstocks, while compositions in the Al–Mg–Er–Zr system (if Zr is available) provide the strongest published Sc-free mechanical performance benchmarks.

| **C — seed 6** | **Al–3Mn–1.5Mg–0.6Cr–0.4Si–0.05Sn** wt% | Combines the most credible apparent-white-space motifs while keeping total solute below 6 wt% and Al well above 85 wt%. | Recommended Zr-free lead: factorially vary Cr 0.3/0.6, Si 0.2/0.4 and Sn 0/0.05; screen density and crack length before tensile testing. | (pqac-00000047, pqac-00000070) |
| **D — atomization atmosphere** | 50–100 vol% N₂, balance noble gas | Airbus claims N₂-rich atomization for Mg–Sc–Zr(–Mn) powder; the proposed few-atomic-layer AlN-rich surface reduces moisture uptake and hydrogen porosity. Conventional Ar/He atomizing gas is described as ≥99.99% pure with H₂O ≤25 ppm. | Copy as an A/B trial only after checking nitride pickup and machine compatibility: high-purity N₂ versus Ar, tightly controlling dew point and oxygen. | (pqac-00000053, pqac-00000054) |
| **D — Mg/Zn compensation** | Feedstock enrichment for volatile solutes | HRL measured approximately 25% Zn and 30% Mg loss under particular LPBF conditions and claims enriched feedstock windows to deliver the target printed composition. | Analyze powder and printed coupons by ICP/OES; determine machine-specific retention before fixing atomized chemistry. Do not apply 25/30% universally. | (pqac-00000045, pqac-00000046) |
| **D — Rusal LPBF starting window** | EOS M290; 280–320 W; 400–1200 mm/s; layers ≤45 μm | Patent worked conditions for the Ni–Mn–Fe–Zr–Ce family yielded low porosity and no hot cracks. | Useful broad DOE bounds for a related eutectic-rich alloy, not a universal recipe for Mg-rich or 7xxx powders. | (pqac-00000011, pqac-00000012) |
| **D — HOT Al LPBF / aging** | 370 W; 1000 mm/s; 0.1 mm hatch; 30 μm layers; 300°C × 5 h | Monash/Amaero’s atomized Al–4.52Mn–1.32Mg–0.79Sc–0.74Zr example reached 577 MPa YS after direct aging. | Copy the direct-aging concept and coupon geometry; do not transfer the energy-density setting unchanged to Sc/Zr-free alloys. | (pqac-00000019, pqac-00000020) |
| **D — melting temperature** | Approximately 700–1000°C | Croteau discloses melting Al–Zn–Mg–Zr alloys with pure elements/master alloys in this range. This is an alloy-making range, **not a validated universal atomization superheat specification**. | Use master alloys for Zr/Cr/Mn, verify complete dissolution, minimize high-temperature hold time and sample the melt before atomization. Establish superheat from each alloy’s liquidus and nozzle behavior rather than adopting 1000°C by default. | (pqac-00000049) |
| **D — unresolved practice gap** | Crucible/refractory selection and ultrasonic small-batch atomization | No retrieved aluminium-alloy source supplied a reliable crucible recommendation or a directly applicable ultrasonic-atomization recipe; the ultrasonic patent recovered concerned heavy metals. | Treat crucible compatibility, Mg oxidation/loss and ultrasonic throughput as experimental process-development questions; avoid presenting them as established patent guidance. | (pqac-00000043, pqac-00000044) |


*Table: Evidence-ranked overlap, apparent white space, Sc-free performance, seed compositions, and process guidance for an LPBF aluminium discovery campaign. “White space” is provisional and requires a formal claim chart and broader freedom-to-operate search.*

info.query:
Survey the PATENT literature and COMMERCIAL products for aluminium alloys designed for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF / SLM) and related powder routes, so that we can choose starting compositions for an alloy discovery campaign and know what is already claimed. We want published compositions, not marketing.

For each entry give: assignee / vendor, product name if any, patent or application numbers (US, EP, WO, CN, JP, DE), priority year, the claimed composition RANGES and the worked EXAMPLE compositions (wt%), the cracking-control and strengthening mechanism claimed, recommended heat treatment, the properties reported in the patent or datasheet (yield, UTS, elongation, hardness, conductivity, test orientation), and whether the patent is granted, pending, expired or abandoned where known.

Cover at least:
1. Airbus / APWorks Scalmalloy (Al-Mg-Sc-Zr-Mn), and the earlier Al-Mg-Sc family patents; lower-Sc or Sc-free variants claimed by others.
2. HRL Laboratories 7A77 and Zr / grain-refiner functionalized 7xxx, 6xxx, 2xxx powders.
3. Aeromet / Aluminium Materials Technologies A20X (A205; Al-Cu-Ag-Mg-Ti-B).
4. NanoAl / Unity Aluminum / Braidy Addalloy (Al-Mg-Zr and others) and Northwestern University Al-Zr-(Er, Sc, Yb, Si) patents.
5. Constellium Aheadd CP1 (Al-Fe-Zr) and HT1 (Al-Ni-Mn-Cu-Zr-Fe class), and the C-TEC patent families (Al-Zr, Al-Fe-Zr, Al-Ni-Zr, Al-Mn-Zr, Al-Cr-Zr).
6. Fehrmann AlMgty (Al-Mg-Si / high-Mg), Rheinfelden (Magsimal, Castasil, Castaduct for AM), AMAG, Hydro, Trimet.
7. Elementum 3D A1000-RAM, A2024-RAM2, A6061-RAM2, A7050-RAM2 (reactive additive manufacturing, in-situ ceramic inoculants).
8. Rusal / IL&M (RS-230, RS-300, RS-320, RS-333, RS-390, RS-553 and similar: Al-Si-Mg-Cu, Al-Mg-Sc, Al-Ni-Mn-Fe-Zr, Al-Cu-Ce), with compositions.
9. Monash University / Amaero high-strength Al-Mn-Sc ("HOT Al"), and Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr.
10. Chalmers / Hoganas Al-Mn-Cr-Zr; Hoganas forAM Al grades; Kymera / ECKA / AP&C / Equispheres / Valimet / Carpenter / Sandvik / Toyal / Eckart (e.g. Eckart TiB2- or Zr-modified, Toyal Hyper-Al) aluminium AM powders with published chemistries.
11. Oak Ridge / Eck Industries / Ames Al-Ce alloys (Al-Ce-Mg, Al-Ce-Ni-Mn, Al-Cu-Mn-Zr / ACMZ, DuAlumin-3D), Lawrence Livermore Al-Ce.
